Thirdly, the dried PbI 2 film was dipped into CH3NH3I solution for 120min, heated at 70 ℃ for 30min to form perovskite.

Herein, we systematically report controllable TiCl 4 processing of the mesoporous TiO2 film and the photovoltaic performance of CH3NH3PbI3-based perovskite devices via two-step sequential deposition procedure. The interconnection of electron transfer materials TiO2 nanocrystalline grain and the roughness of the 5 mesoporous surface can be controlled by varying the TiCl4 processing time. Moreover, time-resolved photoluminescence (TRPL) spectroscopy revealed that electron injection with proper TiCl4 processing is significant, which can effectively suppress charge recombination, thereby enhance the photovoltaic 10 performance for the devices.

unresolved_notes: The source does not explicitly report the device polarity; it was therefore left as not_reported rather than inferred from the ordered layers.

The six TiCl4 processing times are fabrication variants of one shared device design, not separate device families. Their processing times and shared TiCl4-processing conditions are retained on the measured devices.

The source reports IPCE curves with a photocurrent response from 400nm to 800nm and says that the integrated photocurrent is consistent with measured Jsc, but it provides no numeric integrated-current outcome and does not identify which individual Table 1 device produced each curve; therefore no additional individual performance observation was created.
The reported IQE curves provide no device-specific numeric photovoltaic outcome, so they were not represented as performance observations.

SEM, AFM, XRD, UV-vis, PbI2-film, perovskite-film, and TRPL specimens are partial-stack or material-characterization specimens rather than complete photovoltaic devices and were excluded from device-centered records.
No photovoltaic aging or operational-stability outcome is reported in the supplied evidence.

The source passages supplied here do not explicitly state a complete slash-delimited finished-device stack in one passage, so full_stack_raw was left null even though the ordered layers are established across the fabrication passages.
The title is taken from the supplied supplement section heading; the main-paper title was not otherwise supplied.

The IPCE passages report curves for treated solar cells and a shared photocurrent-response range of 400nm to 800nm, but they do not explicitly link an IPCE outcome to any one supported individual device; no PerformanceObservation was created.

The parser text corrupts the coordinated family-level list of mesoporous-TiO2 treatment times with inserted line numbers. The malformed list was removed from the family processing step; the individual treatment times are retained from the unambiguous table row and figure labels.
